topics.name: Baseline assessment
subtopics: Weeks 1-2 are allocated to baseline assessment alongside the content listed for these weeks

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Counting (integrated with number patterns and mental maths)
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number to 60 (weeks 1-2), 80 (weeks 3-6) and 100 (weeks 7-10)
Count forwards and backwards in 10s, 5s and 2s from any multiple within the same ranges; use the relationship between + and -; emphasise more than, less than; ascending and descending order

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Mental maths (number range 25)
subtopics: Order a given set of numbers; compare numbers to 15 (weeks 1-4), 20 (weeks 5-6) and 25 (weeks 7-10) and say which is 1, 2 or 10 more or less
Rapid recall of addition and subtraction facts to 10
Strategies: put the bigger number first to count on or back, number line, doubling or halving, building up or breaking down

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Count objects reliably to 100
subtopics: Count concrete objects reliably to 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 across the term; give a reasonable estimate and check by counting; group counting

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Number symbols and number names
subtopics: Recognise, identify and read number symbols 1-100
Write number symbols and number names to 25

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 25
subtopics: Describe and compare numbers to 25: smaller than, greater than; 1, 2, 3 or 4 more or less
Order numbers from smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value (numbers between 11 and 25)
subtopics: Decompose two-digit numbers into multiples of tens and units/ones to 15 (weeks 1-4), 20 (weeks 5-6) and 25 (weeks 7-10)
Identify and state the value of each digit

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Solve problems in context to 25
subtopics: Addition and subtraction problems (weeks 1-2, 7-10); money problems involving totals and change (weeks 1-4, 9-10)
Repeated addition leading to multiplication (weeks 1-2, 5-6, 9-10)
Equal grouping and sharing leading to division that may include remainders (weeks 3-8)
Techniques: drawings or concrete apparatus, building up and breaking down, doubling and halving, number lines supported with apparatus (CAPS pp. 61-62 problem types)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 20
subtopics: Addition and subtraction to 15 (weeks 1-4) and 20 (weeks 5-10) using +, -, = and □
Practise number bonds to 10
Add the same number repeatedly to 20; multiply numbers 1 to 10 by 2 (link to counting in 2s)

topics.name: Measurement: Time
subtopics: Know the sequence of months of the year; place birthdays on a calendar
Tell 12-hour time in hours and half hours on an analogue clock
Use clocks to calculate length of time in hours and half hours

topics.name: Measurement: Length
subtopics: Estimate, measure, compare, order and record length using non-standard units (hand spans, foot paces, metre stick, string)
Vocabulary: long, longer, longest; short, shorter, shortest

topics.name: Patterns, functions and algebra: Geometric and number patterns
subtopics: Geometric patterns made with objects, drawings of lines and shapes: copy, extend and describe; create and describe own patterns
Number patterns to 150

topics.name: Space and shape: 3D objects
subtopics: Investigate which objects roll or slide (spheres, prisms); straight and curved sides
Use collected waste boxes to describe, sort, compare and stack 3D objects

topics.name: Data handling: Collect, sort, represent and discuss data
subtopics: Collect and sort data (e.g. 2D shapes or 3D objects from weeks 5-6)
Represent sorted data and discuss the sorted collections

topics.name: Revision (weeks 9-10)
subtopics: Weeks 9-10 are labelled REVISION under Numbers, operations and relationships

topics.name: Remediation
subtopics: Supporting learning gaps: reteach using another strategy for improved learning; record findings where further support is required

topics.name: Consolidation
subtopics: Reinforce more of the same (practice) to embed knowledge and skills; give learners the opportunity to ask questions

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Repeat the knowledge and skills taught to establish whether learning has taken place, before new concepts are taught

sba: One formal assessment task (FAT) per term
Weeks 3-4: Measurement; Patterns, functions and algebra (oral)
Weeks 5-6: Numbers, operations and relationships; Patterns, functions and algebra (written); Space and shape (oral/practical)
Weeks 7-8: Numbers, operations and relationships; Measurement; Data handling (written)
Weeks 9-10: Numbers, operations and relationships; Space and shape (written/practical)

topics.name: Diagnostic assessment
subtopics: Weeks 1-2 are allocated to diagnostic assessment alongside the content listed for these weeks

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Counting (integrated with number patterns and mental maths)
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number between 0 and 110 (weeks 1-2), 120 (weeks 3-4), 140 (weeks 5-8) and 150 (weeks 9-10)
Count forwards and backwards in 10s, 5s, 2s, 3s and 4s from any multiple within the same ranges; use the relationship between + and -; emphasise more than, less than; ascending and descending order

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Mental maths (number range 50)
subtopics: Order a given set of numbers; compare numbers to 30 (weeks 1-2), 40 (weeks 3-6) and 50 (weeks 7-10)
Say which is more or less by 1, 2, 10 (weeks 1-2); 1-4 (weeks 3-4); 2, 5, 10 (weeks 5-6); 1-5 and 10 (weeks 7-10)
Rapid recall of addition and subtraction facts to 10

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Count objects reliably to 150
subtopics: Count concrete objects reliably to 100 (weeks 1-2), 120 (weeks 3-4), 140 (weeks 5-6) and 150 (weeks 7-10); estimate and check by counting; group counting

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Number symbols and number names
subtopics: Recognise, identify and read number symbols 1-150
Write number symbols and number names to 50

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 50
subtopics: Describe and compare numbers to 30, 40 and 50 across the term: smaller than, greater than
Order numbers from smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value (numbers between 11 and 50)
subtopics: Decompose two-digit numbers into multiples of tens and units/ones to 30 (weeks 1-2), 40 (weeks 3-6) and 50 (weeks 7-10)
Identify and state the value of each digit

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Solve problems in context to 50
subtopics: Addition and subtraction; repeated addition leading to multiplication; equal grouping and sharing leading to division that may include remainders
Money problems involving totals and change
Techniques: drawings or concrete apparatus, building up and breaking down, doubling and halving, number lines supported with apparatus (CAPS pp. 61-62 problem types)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 50
subtopics: Addition and subtraction to 30 (weeks 1-2), 40 (weeks 3-6) and 50 (weeks 7-10) using +, -, = and □
Practise number bonds to 10 (weeks 1-2), 12 (weeks 3-4) and 15 (weeks 5-10)
Add the same number repeatedly to 30 (weeks 1-2), 40 (weeks 5-6) and 50 (weeks 9-10)
Multiply numbers 1 to 10 by 2 and 5 (weeks 3-10; to 40 in weeks 3-4)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Fractions
subtopics: Thirds and fifths (weeks 3-4)
Recognise fractions in diagrammatic form (weeks 5-6)
Write fractions as 1 half, 2 thirds (weeks 7-8)

topics.name: Measurement: Time
subtopics: Know the sequence of months of the year; place birthdays on a calendar
Tell 12-hour time in hours and half hours on an analogue clock
Use clocks to calculate length of time in hours and half hours (factor in problem solving)

topics.name: Measurement: Mass
subtopics: Estimate, measure, compare, order and record mass using a scale and non-standard measures
Talk about the comparison: light, heavy, lighter, heavier

topics.name: Patterns, functions and algebra: Geometric and number patterns
subtopics: Geometric patterns made with objects, drawings of lines and shapes: copy, extend and describe; create and describe own patterns
Number patterns to 150 (link to purposeful group counting)

topics.name: Space and shape: Position, directions and 2D shapes
subtopics: Language of position: in front of, behind, left, right, up, down, next to, on top of
Position and directions: follow directions to move around the classroom
Recognise, name, describe, sort and compare 2D shapes; range of shapes; features of shapes

subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number between 0 and 150 (weeks 1-2), 160 (weeks 3-4), 170 (weeks 5-6) and 180 (weeks 7-10)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Count objects reliably to 180

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Number symbols and number names
subtopics: Recognise, identify and read number symbols 1-180
Write number symbols and number names to 75

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 75
subtopics: Describe and compare numbers to 50, 60, 70 and 75 across the term: smaller than, greater than
Order numbers from smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value (numbers between 11 and 75)
subtopics: Decompose two-digit numbers into multiples of tens and units/ones to 50 (weeks 1-2), 60 (weeks 3-4), 70 (weeks 5-6) and 75 (weeks 7-10)

Multiply numbers 1 to 10 by 2 and 5 (weeks 1-2, 7-8), 2 and 4 (weeks 3-4), 2, 5 and 4 (weeks 5-6), 4 and 5 (weeks 9-10) using ×, □ and =

topics.name: Measurement: Telling time
subtopics: Name and sequence days of the week and months of the year
Tell 12-hour time in hours, half hours and quarter hours
Use clocks to calculate length of time in hours and half hours

topics.name: Measurement: Capacity
subtopics: Estimate, measure, compare, order and record capacity of containers using non-standard measures
Introduce formal measuring: litre, ml; capacity of commercially packaged objects
Solve word problems in context and explain solutions

Number patterns: copy, extend and describe to 150 (multiples of 10, 5, 2, 3, 4); create own number patterns

topics.name: Data handling: Collect, represent and interpret data

Analyse and interpret data (e.g. litres of milk used by 5 families from Monday to Friday)

subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number between 0 and 180 (weeks 1-4) and 200 (weeks 5-10)
Count forwards and backwards in 10s, 5s, 2s, 3s and 4s from any multiple within the same ranges; use the relationship between + and -; emphasise more than, less than; ascending and descending order

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 99

Order numbers from smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest
Use ordinal numbers to show place or position: first, second, third ... tenth (weeks 3-4, 7-8)
